sections.label: Debt collection reports average
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2021, an average of 367 reports were lodged each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2021, an average of 367 reports were lodged each year.

sections.label: Case for regulating debt collection
sections.summary: A case exists to institute a regime to regulate the debt collection industry and address problematic conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: However, individuals and businesses should not be subjected to debt collection methods that clearly exceed what may be considered reasonable pressure for payment, especially if these methods also affect the public's sense of safety and security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There is thus a case to institute a regime to regulate the debt collection industry and to address problematic debt collection conduct.

sections.label: Regulating and reducing problematic conduct
sections.summary: The Bill aims to regulate the industry through licensing and to reduce problematic conduct through levers against errant parties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: One, to regulate the debt collection industry and prevent problematic debt collection conduct by setting standards of entry into the industry and imposing appropriate licensing requirements on debt collection businesses and debt collectors; and two, to reduce problematic debt collection conduct by putting in place appropriate levers to take errant debt collection businesses and debt collectors to task.

sections.label: Entities covered by Bill
sections.summary: The Bill will regulate debt collection businesses and their debt collectors, and entities primarily in lending and collecting money owed to their own business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To improve oversight of the debt collection industry, the Bill will regulate: one, debt collection businesses, which collect debt from a debtor either on behalf of another person or where the businesses themselves had acquired the debt and their debt collectors; and two, entities carrying on a business which is primarily in the lending of money and collecting of money owed to their own business and which are already regulated by other Government entities today, such as banks and licensed moneylenders.

sections.label: Debt collector deployment approval
sections.summary: An individual deployed as a debt collector must make a joint application with the licensed business and obtain approval before carrying out debt collection activity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: An individual who is deployed as a debt collector by a licensed debt collection business must make a joint application with the debt collection business and must obtain an approval to be so deployed, before he or she can carry out any debt collection activity.

sections.label: Penalties for contravening regulations
sections.summary: Offenders face a fine not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or both, with higher penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For such cases, where a contravention of regulations is made out upon investigations, the offender will be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For repeat offenders, the punishment will increase to a fine not exceeding $20,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

sections.label: Class licensing for regulated businesses
sections.summary: Clauses 6(2), 14 and 15 create a class licensing regime letting already-regulated lending businesses do debt collection without an individual licence if they meet conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clauses 6(2), 14 and 15 set out a class licensing regime for already-regulated businesses whose core business includes lending and collecting money owed to their own business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: They will be allowed to carry out debt collection activities if they comply with the class licensing conditions and they do not need to apply for an individual licence.

sections.label: Offences and penalties under Clause 6
sections.summary: Clause 6 sets offences for unlicensed debt collection business and unlicensed activity by regulated businesses, with fines or imprisonment, higher for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 6 sets out offences for: one, the carrying on of a debt collection business without a valid licence; and two, the conduct of any debt collection activity by an already-regulated business without a valid class licence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Such offences will attract a fine of up to $20,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For repeat offenders, the punishment is a fine of not less than $20,000 and not more than $100,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or both.

sections.label: Fines and imprisonment for offenders
sections.summary: Offenders face a fine up to $10,000 or 12 months' imprisonment, or both; repeat offenders face up to $20,000 or two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Offenders will be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Repeat offenders will be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $20,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

sections.label: Licensing and approval requirements for collectors
sections.summary: Debt collection businesses must obtain a licence and answer for their collectors, who need Police approval, while regulated lenders and their in-house collectors need not apply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Specifically, under this Bill, a debt collection business must apply for and obtain a licence to carry out debt collection activities and be responsible for the conduct of its debt collectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The debt collector must obtain an approval from the Police before they can carry out any debt collection activity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: An already-regulated business that lends and collects money, such as a bank and a licensed or exempted moneylender, need not apply for an individual licence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Its in-house debt collectors will also not be required to apply for approval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: I believe the introduction of this Bill will help to better regulate Singapore's debt collection industry and deter problematic debt collection conduct, while also preserving the public’s sense of safety and security.

sections.label: Police reports on debt collection harassment
sections.summary: The number of Police reports made against debt collection harassment has remained high in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The number of Police reports made against debt collection harassment has remained high in recent years.

sections.label: Online correspondence and debt collection rules
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Bill covers online correspondence, noting US rules on email, text and social media contact and debtor opt-out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Does the Bill cover online correspondences, such as email, social media platforms and instant messaging apps?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These channels have become increasingly common means for debt collectors to badger the debtor, so much so that the US' Consumer Financial Protection Bureau had in 2021 approved a set of rules which dictate how debt collection agencies can email, text or contact debtors on social media to seek repayment of unpaid debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Among these rules, collectors must allow debtors to opt out of being contacted online.

sections.label: Cap on debt collection incentives
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will cap incentives a debt collection company can earn per assignment and whether clients must pay base compensation if targets are unmet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider implementing a cap on the total amount of incentives that a debt collection company can earn from a particular assignment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are clients of debt collection agencies required to pay a base compensation to these agencies even if the agency fails to achieve the target?

sections.label: Community legal clinics and debt collectors
sections.summary: Asks if community legal clinics are adequately equipped, notes debt collectors' intimidation tactics, and says new laws should reduce harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are our community legal clinics adequately equipped to help residents who have relevant concerns?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They shared that the way some of these debt collection agencies work is no different from how some loan sharks or "Ah Longs" operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some have no qualms about using tactics, such as public intimidation, shaming using vulgarities and, sometimes, even using violence to get the work done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Any eventual failure to reclaim debts should be resolved through legal means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am confident that the new laws would greatly reduce the number of harassment cases and, in doing so, help build a safer and secure Singapore.

sections.label: Police reports against debt collectors
sections.summary: MHA pointed out a high number of Police reports against debt collection companies and collectors for activities causing alarm and nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, as MHA pointed out, there has been a high number of Police reports made against debt collection companies and debt collectors for conducting debt collection activities in a manner that caused alarm and nuisance to members of the public.

sections.label: Minister's regulation-making powers
sections.summary: Section 45 states the Minister may make regulations restricting the manner or methods licensees or their debt collectors use to collect debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 45 highlights that the Minister may make regulations for restricting the manner or methods by which a licensee or any of its debt collectors, collect, or attempt to collect, any debt.

sections.label: Debt collector livestreaming debtors
sections.summary: A September 2021 TODAY article reported a debt collection agency livestreamed debt repayment demands and uploaded videos showing debtors' faces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a September 2021 article by TODAY, a particular debt collection agency even publicly shared that they livestreamed themselves demanding debt repayment and uploaded such videos showing the debtors' faces as so-called evidence to protect themselves.

sections.label: Bank's cash advance fees and interest
sections.summary: A new bank claims no cash advance fees but charges an effective interest rate of 26.9% per annum until full repayment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To cite a recent similar but unrelated example, a particular new bank lauds itself for transparency and simplicity and proudly proclaims that there are no cash advance fees for its card.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, there will be an effective interest rate of 26.9% per annum charged from the date of the transaction until the date of full repayment.

sections.label: Compliance officer qualifications and training
sections.summary: Asks what qualifications, experience and training will be required for compliance officers, who can be as young as 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given their significant powers and that they can be as young as 18 years old, it is important that compliance officers are fully ready for their role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what qualifications, experience and training will be required for compliance officers?

sections.label: Penal Code protection for compliance officers
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider extending the Penal Code to protect compliance officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider extending the Penal Code to protect compliance officers?

sections.label: Fit and proper debt collector factors
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for examples of factors used to deem someone fit and proper to be deployed as a debt collector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide examples of what factors may be used to deem if someone is fit and proper to be deployed as a debt collector?

sections.label: Police reports against debt collectors
sections.summary: States MHA's media release cited many Police reports against debt collection companies and collectors for conduct causing alarm and nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to MHA's media release for this Bill, there has been a high number of Police reports against debt collection companies and debt collectors for carrying out debt collection activities in a manner that caused alarm and nuisance to members of the public and MHA is instituting regulations to better manage these disamenities arising from such activities.

sections.label: Debt collection regulations and disputes
sections.summary: Asks whether regulations will let debtors dispute or validate debt information and ensure effective, reasonable debt collection without intimidation or harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: With this in mind, I am, certainly, hoping that the new proposed regime under the Bill will be effective in regulating the conduct of debt collection companies and their staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I also note from MHA's consultation paper to the proposed new regulations that there are eight rules of "dos and don'ts" pertaining to debt collection enforcement and activities by both debt collector individuals and the debt collection companies included at Annex B to the consultation paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the regulations provide debtors with a method for disputing and/or obtaining validation of debt information?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, may I ask how would the Government ensure that the regulations will allow for effective and reasonable debt collection methods that make sense commercially, whilst still able to draw a line to ensure that there is no undesirable intimidation, harassment or conduct?

sections.label: Compliance officer public authority restriction
sections.summary: States Clause 4(1) provides that an appointed compliance officer cannot be an employee of a public authority or a public officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 4(1) of the Bill specifically provides that an individual who is appointed as a compliance officer cannot be an employee of a public authority or a public officer.

sections.label: Unifying codes of practice
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that multiple codes of practice for debt collectors be unified, harmonised and given legal effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, as the Bill allows for the existence of multiple codes of practice which may apply to debt collectors, I propose that the various codes of practice, which may be enacted in legislation and subsidiary legislation, be unified, harmonised and given legal effect.

sections.label: United States debt collection law
sections.summary: The United States Fair Debt Collection Practices Act is a federal law prescribing one singular, unified and legally binding piece of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Taking the United States as an example, their Fair Debt Collection Practices Act is a federal law that prescribes one singular, unified and legally binding piece of legislation.

sections.label: MWS programme and UK debt relief
sections.summary: Methodist Welfare Services matches $2 for every dollar of debt cleared by low-income clients, and UK borrowers may be eligible for Debt Relief Orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A private charity, the Methodist Welfare Services (MWS) developed the MWS Family Development programme, where for every dollar of debt cleared by clients on their own, MWS will match with $2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This programme is targeted at low-income families living on a per capita income of less than $850.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As another reference point, in the UK, borrowers who are unable to repay their debts are, generally, eligible for Debt Relief Orders if they meet criteria, such as owing less than £30,000, having less than £75 a month in spare income and having less than a certain threshold of assets.

sections.label: Disputed debts approach
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the approach would be when debt collection agency staff deal with persons who dispute their debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, what would be the approach when staff of debt collection agencies deal with persons who dispute their debts?

sections.label: Debtors requiring companies to stop
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether alleged debtors can require debt collection staff to stop engaging them and refer cases back to creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In such situations and in the absence of a Court judgment, can the alleged debtors require the staff of debt collection companies to stop engaging them and refer the case back to the creditors?

sections.label: Remit of debt collection companies
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on the remit of debt collection companies under the licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Second and finally, I seek clarification on what will be the remit of the debt collection companies under the licensing regime.

sections.label: Differentiating class licences for moneylenders
sections.summary: MHA is asked whether it will differentiate class licences between MAS-regulated and non-MAS-regulated moneylenders so licensing conditions match each group's risk profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that moneylenders are, generally, less sophisticated, with fewer resources than banks, which are highly regulated, will MHA consider differentiating the class licences, for example, between the institutions that are MAS-regulated versus those that are not, so that licensing conditions are appropriate to the risk profile of the two groups?

sections.label: Ex-offenders as debt collectors
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether ex-offenders who have turned over a new leaf will be allowed to work as security officers and debt collectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One claimed to have had a dated conviction of 15 years ago, has since stayed crime-free and has been proactive in equipping himself with the relevant skills but still was not successful in getting a licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, can the Minister clarify whether ex-offenders who have turned over a new leaf will be given a chance to work as security officers and, specifically to this Bill, as debt collectors in this new regime?

sections.label: Safeguards against false complaints
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether there will be further safeguards against such complaints, beyond Penal Code levers on false information, to be fair to well-conducting debt collectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if there would be further safeguards against such complaints, in addition to levers in the Penal Code relating to the provision of false information, to be fair to debt collection companies or collectors who conduct themselves well?

sections.label: Licensing regime and foreign worker moneylending
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the licensing regime and acceptable debt collection methods, and asks MHA to look into moneylending involving foreign workers, including migrant domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some collectors do harass their targets and those around them, such as family members, neighbours and co-workers, in attempts to get the attention of the borrowers and pressurise them to pay up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need to put a stop to these wrongful practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the proposed legislation to set up a licensing regime and specify what the acceptable debt collection methods will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would also like to take this opportunity to request that MHA look into the moneylending activities involving foreign workers, including migrant domestic workers.

sections.label: Fit and proper licensing criteria
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill is timely and its licensing regime ensures those involved are fit and proper, but asks what criteria Police would use to assess applicants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There were also incidents where residents were tricked into borrowing and then subjected to exorbitant interest charges and their repayment refused; and cases where the wrong parties are mistakenly identified and pursued by the debt collector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, Sir, the Debt Collection Bill is, therefore, timely to improve visibility and oversight of the debt collection industry and deter problematic debt-collecting behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The licensing regime introduced under the Bill, to ensure that those involved are fit and proper, would go some way to hold those involved in debt collection accountable for their debt collection activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, it is unclear what specific criteria the Police would use to assess the applicants as fit and proper.

sections.label: Definition of regulated debt
sections.summary: The Bill defines debt as a monetary obligation owed by a debtor, and collection of such debts, secured or unsecured, will be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Bill defines debt as a monetary obligation owed by a debtor; the collection of such debts, whether secured or unsecured, will be regulated.

sections.label: Debt collectors verifying and stopping collection
sections.summary: Debt collectors must verify the debtor owes the debt and must stop collecting if the debt is disputed or being settled elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For example, debt collectors will be required to verify that the subject of the debt collection from whom they are attempting to collect a debt, indeed owes the debt, such as verifying the subject's identity against the signatory to a debt contract.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Debt Collection Regulations will also prohibit debt collectors from continuing to collect debt from a debtor if the debtor has informed the debt collection business or collector that the debt is in dispute or that the debtor has initiated a process to settle the debt through other means.

sections.label: No code of practice; proof of approval
sections.summary: Regulations will guide debt collection conduct, so no code of practice is planned, and debt collectors must show proof of the Licensing Officer's approval when asked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Given that there will be regulations to guide the conduct of debt collection businesses and their debt collectors, we do not intend to issue a code of practice for now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To address Mr Leon Perera and Mr Yip Hon Weng's question about how debtors may verify the legitimacy of debt collectors, we will require debt collectors to show proof of the Licensing Officer's approval, when asked to do so.

sections.label: Written notice before regulatory action
sections.summary: The Licensing Officer must give written notice and at least 14 days for written representations before taking regulatory action against a licensee or debt collector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Before regulatory action can be taken against the licensee or debt collector, the Licensing Officer must first give a written notice to the licensee or the debt collector and provide at least 14 days after the written notice is served, for written representations to be made to the Licensing Officer with respect to the proposed regulatory action.

sections.label: Borrowing from licensed entities, public vigilance
sections.summary: The public should borrow only from licensed entities and be vigilant with personal particulars and banking credentials, and the Bill will improve debt collection conduct.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Members of the public who wish to take up loans should only borrow from licensed entities, such as banks, financial institutions and licensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We also encourage members of the public to be vigilant and exercise due care before furnishing personal particulars and banking credentials for any purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Bill will help improve the conduct of the debt collection industry and better address disamenities that may arise from problematic debt collection conduct.
